title: Moments Before Chaos Erupts at Target
description:
MIDWEST SAFETY: Uncover. Inform. Empower.

Please consider JOINING for $1 a month. It *really* helps us do original reporting like this. 

MERCH! Midwest-Safety.com

CONTACT US:
Complaints? Video submissions? Tips? Sponsorships? Collabs? Business inquires? 
Email our board at mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com. 

BE NICE:
The individuals presented in these videos may be suffering from the effects of alcohol, drug abuse, a mental health disorder or simply having a bad day. The videos should NOT be presumed to be representative of their general behavior. Everyone deserves to be treated with respect. 

RIGHT TO BE FORGOTTEN:
Midwest Safety practices the "Right to be Forgotten." If you were the suspect in a lower-level offense, you may email our board to request removal. 
Email: mn.safety.alerts@gmail.com

The two shoplifting males were found to not be associated with each other, despite the thefts taking place at the same exact target on the same day, just hours apart. Reports indicate the male who stole the shoes, was involved in 48 prior theft incidents at other regional targets in previous years. He was given a citation for theft in the third degree and was transported to jail without incident. The other male who fled in his vehicle was also charged with theft in the third degree, as well as reckless driving, one count of hit and run to an attended vehicle, and two counts of hit and run to an unattended vehicle. Both suspects are innocent unless proven guilty in a court of law these shoplifters are trying to turn target into their own personal playground but when are they going to learn that technology is only getting better these criminals don't understand that today's stores are not just relying on security guards and regular cameras anymore to turn into solar power cellular license plate readers that stand vehicles in real time and instantly alert store security to known suspects or repeat offenders and the result is precision alerts and faster response times and some retailers say that these systems pay for themselves within hours and in a world where criminals move fast these stores are learned to move faster because we've got one guy who calmly strolls out like shoplifting is his daily occupation, which it probably is. Only to get found and quickly tased at a gas station, it seems like these criminals all go to the same school of stupidity, because most of them always try to feign ignorance. And just as officers are closing in on one suspect who slammed into police, another man enters the same target like he's filling in for the last guy. And this isn't just petty theft, it's about patterns because these people are getting bolder, more coordinated, and more reckless. And they know that cameras are watching, they just don't care, and they'll hurt police or another shopper just to get away. And in this last case timing was everything, and without quick action from officers and alert store staff, the second suspect might have walked off just as cleanly as the first. But thankfully, technology and sharp police work did turn the tables this time, but next time it might be a different store and different outcome. But in my opinion, the only thing more dangerous than people who steal are those are willing to hurt people to get away.
